title: Compactness of a minimax sublevel set
statement: Let $X \subseteq \bbr$ be compact, fix a payoff function $f : \bbr \times \bbr \to \bbr$, a column point $y \in \bbr$, and a threshold $c \in \bbr$, and suppose the map $x \mapsto f(x,y)$ is continuous on $X$. Then the minimax sublevel set $\mathrm{sublevel}(X,f,y,c) = X \cap \{x \in \bbr : f(x,y) \le c\}$ is compact.
hypotheses_covered: x ↦ f(x,y) is continuous on X
fixed column point y and threshold c
replaced:
If $X$ is compact and $f(\cdot,y)$ is continuous on $X$, then
$\mathrm{sublevel}(X,f,y,c)$ is compact (as a closed subset of a compact set).
